metadata.title: Bookmark Scout – Save bookmarks to the right folder, fast
metadata.description: Browser extension that saves pages to the right bookmark folder: type a folder name, press a shortcut, or let AI suggest one. Plus search and cleanup.

features: Save to a folder by typing its name
Quick save shortcut with an in-page notification and undo
Side panel support (the sidebar in Firefox)
Undo and redo in the bookmarks manager
Bookmarks manager that works like Chrome's
Dead link scanning with reviewed repairs
Privacy review with optional redaction before exports
Opt-in AI chat that changes bookmarks only after you approve
Local AI agents through an MCP server, with approvals

languageSuggestion.label: Language suggestion
languageSuggestion.text: This page is also available in English.

footer.tagline: Save pages to the right folder, then find and tidy them, right in your browser.
footer.madeBy: Made by {author}. Free and open source.

hero.title: Save every page to the right folder, in seconds.
hero.description: Type part of a folder's name, or press {{SHORTCUT:commands.quick-save}} on any page, and the page is saved to the folder it belongs in. Opt-in AI can suggest the folder too. Bookmark Scout also searches and tidies the bookmarks you already have, in Chrome, Edge, and Firefox, with no account and no server of its own.
hero.demoNote: This demo uses a made-up folder tree and keeps nothing. The extension shows your own folders, inside your browser.

demo.label: Try it: save this page to a folder
demo.placeholder: Type part of a folder name
demo.startHint: Type a few letters of a folder name. Matching folders appear here, nested ones included.
demo.alreadySaved: Already in {folder}, so it was not saved twice.
demo.emptyHint: Try part of a folder name, or a path such as travel/japan. A word of 4 letters or more may have one typo.

tour.title: What you can do with it
tour.lede: Real screenshots from the Chrome build. They follow your system's light or dark setting.
tour.firefoxNote: Firefox cannot replace its bookmarks page, so in Firefox the manager, with its cleanup tools, saved searches, and import and export, opens from a button in the toolbar popup.

save.heading: Save to the right folder
save.caption: The toolbar popup: type part of a folder's name, or pick a folder in the tree, and save the page in one click.
save.alt: Two popups: "pas" typed in the search box with the Pasta folder (Recipes / Italian) selected under Save to folder, and AI suggestions for the current page: the existing Recipes/Italian/Pasta folder and a new Recipes/Quick Dinners folder
points: Type part of a folder's name, even one nested deep in the tree, and save the current page there without leaving the keyboard
Type a path such as work/react, and still find the folder with a small typo
Press {{SHORTCUT:commands.quick-save}} on any page to save it to the folder that matches it best; a small notification in the page offers Undo and other folders
A page already in that folder is not saved twice, and folders you saved to recently come first
Save links from the right-click menu into recent folders
With AI turned on, get folder suggestions for the page, or save to the first one with {{SHORTCUT:commands.ai-quick-save}}

organize.heading: Find and organize what you saved
organize.caption: The manager replaces Chrome's Bookmarks page and works like it, with a folder tree, breadcrumbs, and a sortable table.
organize.alt: The Bookmark Scout manager showing the Dev Docs folder as a table with type, folder path, URL, title, and date added columns next to a folder tree
points: Search every bookmark as you type, with match case, whole word, and regular expression options
Keep the same tree and search open in the browser's side panel (the sidebar in Firefox)
Save a search as a smart view that always shows current results
Select rows with Shift and Ctrl, right-click for cut, copy, paste, and open all, and drag rows, folders, and links where they belong
Undo and redo changes with {{SHORTCUT:manager.undo}} and {{SHORTCUT:manager.redo}} ({{SHORTCUT_MAC:manager.undo}} and {{SHORTCUT_MAC:manager.redo}} on a Mac), even after a reload
Import HTML or JSON after a preview, and export HTML, JSON, Markdown, or CSV
Link to a folder or a search, and move through it all with the keyboard

cleanUp.heading: Tidy years of saved links
cleanUp.caption: Duplicate Cleaner shows each group and the copy it keeps before anything is removed.
cleanUp.alt: The Duplicate Cleaner dialog listing two groups of duplicate bookmarks, each with the copy to keep marked, above a Remove duplicates button
points: Review duplicate groups, then remove the extra copies
Strip tracking parameters from URLs after a preview
Find dead links and repair them: delete, use the redirect, point to an archived copy, or edit the URL
Fetch page titles and apply only the ones you pick
Download each site's own icon, so bookmarks show it even in Firefox
Undo deletions and cleanups from the message that follows

ai.heading: Use AI with your own provider, or not at all
ai.caption: AI is off until you turn it on in Settings, choose a provider, and add your own API key where the provider needs one.
ai.alt: The AI tab of the Bookmark Scout settings page with AI features turned off, and provider and model selectors
points: Ask AI about your bookmarks: it searches them, checks links, and proposes moves, renames, and new folders as a plan that changes nothing until you approve it
Let AI agents on your computer, such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor, look up bookmarks through an MCP server, and approve each change they ask for in the browser
Tag suggestions and short summaries that you review before saving
Folder reorganization plans, previewed before anything moves, with undo
Export selected bookmarks as Markdown or XML context for an AI chat; this works without AI and sends nothing

diagram.legend: Dashed paths are optional. They open only when you use that feature.

noServer.title: No account, no server
noServer.body: There is nothing to sign up for, and Bookmark Scout has no server of its own. Your bookmarks are read and changed inside your browser.

noTelemetry.title: No telemetry
noTelemetry.body: The extension sends nothing to the developer: no analytics, no ads, no tracking.

aiOptIn.title: AI is off until you turn it on
aiOptIn.body: Requests then go straight from your browser to the provider you chose. With Ollama on your own computer, they stay there. Local AI agents get nothing until you allow them, and their changes wait for your approval.

exports.title: Exports get a privacy review
exports.body: Before a file downloads, a review flags tokens, email addresses, and other sensitive values, and can redact them in the copy you save.

install.title: Install it in a few steps
install.lede: Pick your browser. Each release on GitHub has a build for Chrome, Edge, and Firefox.
install.storeComing: The {store} listing is being prepared. Until it is live, install the build from GitHub Releases.
install.manual: Or install the build from GitHub Releases yourself:

steps.download: Download bookmark-scout-*-chrome.zip from the latest release and extract it.
steps.open: Open chrome://extensions and turn on Developer mode in the top right.
steps.load: Click Load unpacked and select the extracted folder.

chrome.crx: The release also has a signed .crx file that you can drag onto the extensions page instead.

steps.download: Download bookmark-scout-*-edge.zip from the latest release and extract it.
steps.load: Click Load unpacked and select the extracted folder.

steps.download: Download bookmark-scout-*-firefox.zip from the latest release and extract it.
steps.load: Click Load Temporary Add-on and select manifest.json in the extracted folder.

firefox.limits: Firefox removes a temporary add-on when it restarts, so you load it again after each restart. In Firefox, the manager and its tools open from the Open bookmark manager button in the toolbar popup.

data.q: Does Bookmark Scout send my bookmarks anywhere?
data.a: No. Your bookmarks are read and changed inside your browser, and the extension sends nothing to the developer. Data leaves your browser only when you use an optional feature: AI requests go to the provider you chose, the dead link checker, title fetcher, and site icon refresh request the bookmarked sites after you allow website access, and local AI agents you allow get what they look up through a program on your computer. Settings sync through your browser account if browser sync is on. The <privacy>privacy policy</privacy> has the details.

needAi.q: Do I need to use AI?
needAi.a: No. Search, organizing, cleanup, and import and export all work without it. AI stays off until you turn it on in Settings.

providers.q: Which AI providers can I use?
providers.a: You can use {providers}. You add your own API key where the provider needs one, and the provider may charge for usage.

changes.q: Will it change my bookmarks without asking?
changes.a: No. Duplicate cleanup, URL cleanup, dead link repairs, fetched titles, AI reorganization, and imports all show a review before anything is written. Ask AI and local AI agents show their changes as a plan and wait for your approval. Deleting asks for confirmation by default, and the bookmarks manager can undo changes with {{SHORTCUT:manager.undo}} ({{SHORTCUT_MAC:manager.undo}} on a Mac).

firefox.a: Yes. Firefox cannot replace its bookmarks page, so the manager, with its cleanup tools, import and export, and saved searches, opens from a button in the toolbar popup. Until the Firefox Add-ons listing is ready, Firefox loads it as a temporary add-on, which is removed when Firefox restarts.

stores.q: Why is it not in the browser stores yet?
stores.a: Listings for the Chrome Web Store, Edge Add-ons, and Firefox Add-ons are being prepared, and each store reviews an extension before it goes live. Until then, install it from GitHub Releases.

free.a: Yes. Bookmark Scout is free and open source under {license}, with no ads and no paid plan. If you turn on AI, your provider may charge for API usage.

help.a: Start with the <support>support page</support> or the <docs>documentation</docs>. You can also report a problem on <github>GitHub</github> or email <email>{supportEmail}</email>.
